standard_prerequisites.name: M tensor K is a finite dimensional vector space for a finite module M over a domain

core_obligations: Prove the easy direction: a submodule of R^{n} over a domain has no torsion element (proof line 4871).
For the converse, pass to the fraction field: M tensor K is a finite dimensional K-vector space, choose a basis e_1 to e_r and generators x_1 to x_n of M (proof lines 4872-4875).
Write every generator as x_i = sum (a_ij/b_ij) e_j with b_ij nonzero and clear all denominators at once by setting b to the product of the b_ij (proof lines 4876-4877).
Use injectivity of M to M tensor K, which is torsion freeness, to conclude that M embeds into the finite free module R e_1/b plus ... plus R e_r/b (proof lines 4878-4880).
proof_roadmap: Interval comparison against the 57 public records of more-algebra.tex: no recorded interval covers 4863-4881. The nearest records are 336 (4721-4764, tag 0H7R) and 337 (5577-5633, tag 0AVB, reflexive modules and codimension-one intersections); the latter is the closest in spirit in the published set (it also studies finiteness properties of modules over a domain) but it concerns reflexive modules and codimension-one intersections, not torsion freeness versus submodules of a finite free module.
difficulty_reason: The lemma is an internal characterisation of finite torsion free modules over a domain, and the content is entirely in one direction (statement lines 4863-4867). The proof has to pass from the abstract module M to a concrete inclusion into a finite free module by choosing a basis of the finite dimensional K-vector space M tensor K, writing the finitely many generators of M in that basis with coefficients in K, clearing the finitely many denominators with one common element b, and then observing that torsion freeness is exactly what makes M embed into R e_1/b plus ... plus R e_r/b (proof lines 4870-4881). The two non-formal points are that a single denominator works for all generators at once and that the resulting map is injective precisely because M is torsion free; neither follows from finiteness alone.
